title: Probability Calculation Methodology
overview: Probability measures the likelihood of events occurring, ranging from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). Fundamental concepts include combinations, permutations, and the rules of probability.

methods.name: Basic Probability
methods.description: The ratio of favorable outcomes to total possible outcomes for equally likely events.

formula.name: Classical Probability
formula.expression: P(A) = Number of favorable outcomes / Total possible outcomes

methods.name: Combinations (nCr)
methods.description: Number of ways to choose r items from n items where order doesn't matter.
methods.bestFor: Lottery odds, committee selection, card hands

methods.name: Permutations (nPr)
methods.description: Number of ways to arrange r items from n items where order matters.

methods.name: Probability Rules
methods.description: Rules for combining probabilities of multiple events.

formula.name: Addition and Multiplication Rules
formula.expression:
Addition (OR): P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B)
Mutually exclusive: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B)

Multiplication (AND): P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B|A)
Independent events: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B)

variables.meaning: Probability of B given A occurred

sources.name: Kolmogorov, A.N. - Foundations of Probability Theory

footnotes: Lottery odds: Powerball is ~1 in 292 million
Gambler's fallacy: past outcomes don't affect independent future events
disclaimer: Probability calculations assume specified conditions hold. Real-world outcomes may be affected by factors not captured in the model.
